page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across several compute and memory metrics. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2140.0 and a multi-core score of 19924.0, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Its memory subsystem demonstrates uncached large-block read bandwidth of 232.42 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 100.8 GB/sec. In specialized tasks, the processor's support for advanced vector and matrix extensions contributes to top-tier performance in image processing and small-model LLM text generation, which reaches 342.39 tokens/sec. However, single-core stress-ng performance and large-model text generation remain in the average tier.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial 2835 GB local storage, the D48ds_v6 offers high resource density for workloads requiring a mix of compute, memory, and fast local disk access. It is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by its strong Passmark database score and Redis throughput of 67.91 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include software compilation, web serving, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.
